title: Canonical supported ordinary scalar quotient tower and marked descent data
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative topological ring, with the all-continuous condensed coefficients and their ordinary internal module categories [sk-def-localizing-closure], [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], [def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. On small pro-etale and etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-size-convention], define multiplication by $a$ from the regular module and monoidal point inverse image. Define $M/\pi^{n+1}$ as its ordinary cokernel and the actual quotient transitions, forming a strict inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system]. Use the full category of finite constant scalar local models [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and the actual composite of open extension by zero and closed direct image along a finite qcqs open-closed path [def-sfb-qcqs-open-closed-tree]. Define its supported quotient tower and augmentation by applying that composite. Scalar coordinates are exact additive functors to module-valued sheaves with an underlying-abelian-sheaf identification and with scalar multiplication fixed on every section. Define marked descent as a functor of finite models to strict etale module towers, with comparison inverse image identified with this supported quotient tower [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], killed by the specified positive power of $\pi$ and some power of $\ell$, and unique up to unique isomorphism preserving this identification. Define scalar-coordinate pullback by its underlying normalized direct-image comparison and adjunction mate. Finally define the actual restriction on sections and its universal right-derived map, the corresponding strict tower comparison, and the canonical map from derived sections to total derived inverse limit of tower sections using the derived constant/limit adjunction [def-weil-derived-limit]. Resolution data record existence on the same ordinary module and strict tower categories, and are never assumed in the reconstruction theorem. Canonical endpoint normalization is equality of maps to the entire derived inverse limit, comparing the actual quotient augmentation with the marked finite comparison, with the ordinary degree-zero normalization at the pulled-back endpoint.
